title: GreenLiver: Randomized study on the influence of intraoperative ICG fluorescence imaging on the R0 resection rate in minimally invasive liver resection
summary:
This study investigates whether ICG fluorescence helps surgeons 
better detect malignant tumors and remove them more precisely during minimally invasive liver surgery. To do this, a dye (indocyanine green, or ICG for short) is administered intravenously a few days before the operation. Under special lighting, tumor tissue can then be highlighted for visibility.
The aim is to improve the quality of the surgery, increase complete tumor removal, 
and reduce the risk of recurrence.
conditions: Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct

interventions.name: Intraoperative ICG fluorescence imaging (0.5 mg/kg IV, administered 3-7 days preoperatively); fluorescence-guided minimally invasive liver resection.
Standard minimally invasive liver resection without ICG administration

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically or radiologically confirmed primary or secondary liver malignancy
- Planned minimally invasive liver resection (robotic or laparoscopic)
- Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 45 mL/min/1.73 m²
- Existence of a written informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
• Allergy or hypersensitivity to indocyanine green (ICG) or iodine-containing 
substances
• Known hyperthyroidism or functional/autonomous thyroid disease
• Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 45 mL/min/1.73 m²
• Child–Pugh C liver cirrhosis
• Technically or functionally unresectable tumors
• Severe cognitive impairment affecting the ability to give informed consent
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
• Participation in another interventional study
